description.narrative: UAE’s National Air Quality Agenda 2031 identifies improvement of indoor air quality (IAQ) and reduction of health risks associated to IAQ pollution as one of the four strategic objectives. Given that the UAE’s population spends majority of their daily hours indoors, good air quality is of high importance. While federal building regulations sets certain standards related to IAQ, the UAE currently does not have in place federal regulations that relate to IAQ. Along with this gap, the Air Quality Agenda identifies other gaps related to IAQ, including lack of comprehensive standards guiding building maintenance activities; absence of a defined framework of responsibilities and lack of public awareness. The National Air Quality Agenda sets out key goals through which to achieve the strategic goal of improving IAQ, including an analysis of existing standards and benchmarking with best practices. Against this background, MOCCAE, in line with the UAE National Air Quality Agenda 2031, intends to generate in-depth evidence on the status of IAQ in the UAE. IAQ has various impacts on the health of UAE’s population, however, data on the state of IAQ across the country is limited. Furthermore, currently the UAE does not have national-level guidelines for IAQ. Using the evidence that will be generated from the IAQ measurement campaign, MOCCAE seeks to build a basis for future IAQ guidelines in the country and has requested GGGI to support in undertaking this work.
